sources.full: Trouble at Grog's — Hall Qualification Conversion

contents.name: Chapter 3: Return to the Happy Orc

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: Three-hour Hall one-shot. Baseline: four 6th-level PCs. Supported range: levels 4–8 and mixed-level tables. Characters may use 2014 or 2024 player rules; this file uses classic 5eTools monster references where practical. Use the closest 2024 equivalent at the table when preferred.

Run three substantive investigation beats. Essential clues are redundant and fail forward. Combat is required, but the finale is objective-based: secure evidence, prevent escape or destruction, capture Yuri, or force surrender. Character death is possible but should be unlikely.
Do not make the players visit every location. Once they have two independent links to Yuri, or one strong link plus a route into his operation, they have enough to move toward the finale.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: Grog is an orc retired adventurer who owns the popular Happy Orc. Yuri Kinnon, owner of the Dagger Rock Tavern, is the sole mastermind behind a staged crime wave intended to frame Grog and other orcs while discrediting Captain Sid Barrow.

Yuri uses Rin and Ellie Felan as his principal thieves and infiltrators, Caela Fourfingers as a spy inside Grog's kitchen, Jim Ramsey as a rumor-spreader and courier, Grunt and Brock as planted mercenaries, and coerced townsfolk connected to the tunnel network.

Sid Barrow is Grog's close friend and strongest official ally. Mayor Wes Jacobs, merchant Berik Anden, and blacksmith Logan Ironhand sit on the council with Sid and Yuri. They are not conspirators and can be moved by evidence.

entries.name: Dagger Rock
entries: Dagger Rock is a small Sword Coast town in Faerûn on a minor trade road between Waterdeep and Neverwinter. Keep travel between local sites abstract so the investigation stays focused on decisions instead of transit.

Preserve the original adventure's comic tone and prejudice theme. The Happy Orc can be rowdy, bawdy, cheap, generous, and funny. The hostility aimed at Grog and other orcs should feel unfair and consequential; Yuri is exploiting prejudice, not proving it correct.

entries.name: The Conspiracy

entries.caption: Conspiracy
rows: Sole mastermind; wants Grog pushed out and Sid discredited.
Principal thieves/infiltrators; live beneath Yuri's tavern.
Kitchen spy planted inside the Happy Orc.
Coerced dwarf mason and tunnel witness.

entries: The hidden tunnels connect multiple town locations. Tunnel evidence proves organized secret activity, but it should be paired with testimony, records, payments, or stolen property before it becomes a complete case against Yuri.

entries.caption: Real-Time Session Clock
rows: Character introductions and arrival at the Happy Orc.
Meet Grog, experience the tavern, hear the problem.
Three investigation beats, about 10–15 minutes each.
Decision checkpoint; Sid hard lead only if needed.
Approach Yuri, tunnels, council, or infiltration.
Reveal map, set positions, move to initiative.

entries.name: Emergency Pacing
entries: At 0:45 without a useful clue: surface the stable-fire evidence or make Grunt/Brock visibly react to the investigation.
At 1:00 without a Yuri link: expose whichever connection follows most naturally—Caela's movement, Grunt/Brock's employer, Jim's trail, or Sid's inventory discrepancy.
At 1:15: summarize the facts aloud. If the PCs still lack a viable route, Sid supplies the hard lead.
At 1:20: stop opening new optional investigation locations. From here, player choices determine how they approach Yuri.
By 1:40: use Sid's hard lead or another fail-forward clue so the PCs have achieved enough success to threaten Yuri; then let Yuri's reaction move the story into the finale.
At 1:50: initiative should be underway.
At 2:30: losing enemies surrender, bargain, or flee. Resolve the objective instead of grinding remaining hit points.
At 2:45: narrate consequences and close on Grog.
{@b Escalation rule.} Use at most two escalation events before the finale. An escalation replaces a slow investigation beat; it does not get added on top of the planned three beats.

entries.caption: Core Cast
rows: Publicly composed businessman; privately controlling mastermind.
Principal thief; prioritizes Ellie and escape.

entries.name: Maps
entries: Use one main physical map for the entire session: the Happy Orc main floor. Leave it on the table from the opening scene onward. The same build can support social play, investigation returns, and the finale.

If desired, keep two small supplemental builds off to the side: an 8 × 6 Stable / Yard and an 8 × 6 Tunnel Chamber (Cellar Entrance). These only come out if the climax spills beyond the tavern proper.

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: Introduce Dagger Rock, Grog, the framing problem, and the first set of leads in about 25–30 minutes. The Happy Orc map should already be visible because it is both the opening location and the likely final battlefield.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: The Happy Orc should feel loud, inexpensive, generous, rowdy, and slightly chaotic rather than sinister. Preserve some bawdy tavern comedy, but do not make Grog a joke.
Grog enjoys playing against his intimidating appearance. Let him startle obvious adventurers before welcoming them warmly.
Show at least one visible sign that anti-orc hostility has real consequences—graffiti, muttered comments, a broken sign, a denied delivery, or another small act of discrimination.
On the physical table, only place pieces you actually own: modular walls plus AF634A furniture, with one custom cellar-entrance marker if you want the underground access visibly represented.

entries.name: Adventure
entries: The PCs arrive in Dagger Rock as strangers and choose the Happy Orc for food or lodging. Give each player a brief introduction before Grog approaches.

entries.name: Arriving in Dagger Rock
entries: Rumors blame orcs and Grog's circle for theft, arson, and intimidation, but the stories disagree about times, witnesses, and details. Treat rumors as leads, never as proof.

entries.name: The Happy Orc
entries: Key staff include Sev Ronan, Julia Ronan, Shod, and Caela Fourfingers. Grunt and Brock have planted themselves around the inn.
If the PCs investigate Grog or his staff first, allow it. They may discover normal tavern problems or petty misconduct by individual patrons, but nothing connecting Grog to the organized crime wave.
Because this same map may host the finale, keep enough open floor space for combat movement even during the opening scene.

entries.name: Meeting Grog
entries: Grog is physically intimidating but warm, direct, and self-aware. He does not demand that the PCs trust him. He is willing to let them check his story.

entries.name: Grog's Problem
entries: Grog says a string of crimes has been blamed on orcs and people associated with his establishment. He believes someone is framing them.
He asks the PCs to look into it because they are new to town and therefore less tangled in local loyalties. Sid Barrow believes Grog's character but needs evidence before acting against anyone.

entries.caption: Initial Leads
rows: Deliberate arson, Shod's observations, Grunt/Brock, Caela.
Crime inventory and contradictions between verified evidence and rumor.
Payment and reporting link to Yuri.
Rumor network, courier behavior, and graveyard tunnel route.

entries.name: Rewards / Transition
entries: Once the players choose a lead, begin the three-beat investigation. Do not make them clear every lead.

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: The investigation should establish three things: the crimes are staged, Yuri's network is involved, and the PCs have a route into the hidden operation. Target 45–55 minutes.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: Run three substantive beats unless the players solve the case sooner. Each beat should answer at least one player question and create a new actionable choice.

Every investigation scene ends with a concrete, actionable next lead. Give the players a person to question, a place to go, an object to compare, or a route to follow—not merely a suspicious impression. Examples: Jim uses the graveyard route; Caela rents a room above the Green Grape; the masonry points to Cal Stone; a conspirator heads toward Yuri's sphere; or stolen property matches Sid's inventory.
Use DC 12 for cooperative information, DC 14 for guarded witnesses, and DC 16 for frightened accomplices or subtle evidence. Do not roll when a player's method logically reveals the information.
A failed check never deletes an essential clue. It can cost time, raise suspicion, produce an incomplete clue, require protection/payment, or add a complication.

entries.name: Adventure

entries.caption: Investigation Beat Budget
rows: Establish that a crime is staged or someone around Grog is compromised.
Establish a concrete Yuri, agent, or tunnel link.
Corroborate the theory or find the route to Yuri's operation.
At 1:15, restate the facts. If needed, Sid supplies the hard lead.

entries: Enough to move to the finale: two independent Yuri links, or one strong Yuri link plus a route into the hidden operation.

entries.name: Sid Barrow
entries: Arrival: Sid is busy, tired, and clearly frustrated by pressure to blame Grog before the evidence supports it.
What he has: a written inventory of recently stolen goods and notes on which eyewitness claims actually match verified facts.

Concrete hard lead: among the stolen goods is a silver-inlaid merchant's compass with a chipped green enamel lid. A witness saw an elf matching Rin's description trying to sell one near Yuri's tavern. Sid will not call this proof, but if the PCs are stuck it gives them a defensible route toward Rin, Ellie, and Yuri.
What he needs: two independent Yuri links are enough for Sid to treat Yuri as a formal suspect and support a lawful search or arrest where circumstances justify it.

If the PCs ask about tunnels, hidden construction, unusual masonry, or who in town could have built such passages, Sid points them to Cal Stone. Sid knows Cal is a local dwarf mason who recently took unusual off-the-books work and has been visibly nervous since.
On failure: Sid withholds speculation, not facts. The PCs still get the inventory and verified timeline.
Next leads: Rin/Ellie through the stolen-goods comparison, or Cal Stone if the PCs pursue the tunnel-construction angle.

entries.name: Stable Fire
entries: Arrival: scorched boards, a cut or loosened lantern bracket, and a strong smell of accelerant make the fire look wrong to anyone who examines the scene.
Shod cannot speak, but he can communicate by gesture, drawing, or leading the PCs to what he noticed. He saw Grunt and Brock near the stable shortly before the fire.
Speak with Animals can shorten the scene: a frightened horse remembers two familiar men, smoke before open flame, and one man dropping something that smelled sharp and oily.
On a failed check, the PCs still learn the fire was deliberate; the cost is that the exact link to Grunt/Brock is less certain until another clue corroborates it.
Next lead: Grunt and Brock. Their presence around the stable gives the PCs specific people to watch, question, follow, or confront.

entries.name: Grunt and Brock
entries: They initially act like rough regulars with no interest in the investigation. If watched, they watch the PCs back.
Pressure response: they may tail the party, search a room, threaten a witness, or try to lure the PCs somewhere private before they choose open violence.
If captured or convincingly cornered, they identify Yuri as the employer behind the arson/intimidation work. They know only part of the larger scheme.

If followed instead of captured, either man can lead the PCs toward Jim, Caela, Yuri's tavern, or a handoff involving Rin or Ellie. If pressured about the tunnels, one can mention the frightened dwarf mason Yuri forced to do the stonework, pointing to Cal Stone.
If the PCs defeat them in a full resource-draining fight, use the Resource Check in Appendix C before the finale.
Next leads: Yuri directly through their testimony; Jim/Caela/Rin/Ellie through surveillance; or Cal through the tunnel-work connection.

entries.name: Caela Fourfingers
entries: Caela is Yuri's spy inside Grog's kitchen. Her nickname is literal: one hand is missing a finger, an easy identifying detail if the PCs have been told to look for her.
Her initial posture is competent employee first, offended suspect second. She does not volunteer guilt.
Concrete clue: she carries or keeps access to a folded payment chit marked with Yuri's tavern account sign and a short coded instruction identifying shifts at the Happy Orc.
Following Caela or intercepting one of her reports can reveal a handoff toward Yuri's tavern or to Rin/Ellie, giving the PCs a route to the principal thieves even if they never visit Sid.
If exposed early, she lies, bolts, or tries to warn Yuri. Do not make the clue vanish: the payment chit, her room, or another agent can preserve the Yuri link.
Next leads: her rented room above the Green Grape, Yuri through the payment chit, or Rin/Ellie through a report handoff.

entries.name: Jim Ramsey
entries: Jim poses as a talkative drunk and repeats the same anti-Grog stories with suspicious consistency.
Observable behavior: he watches who reacts to the rumors, leaves by a side route after asking leading questions, and periodically checks a small waxed-paper message packet hidden inside his coat.
Following him can lead to the graveyard entrance or a rendezvous connected to Yuri. Pressuring him can expose the rumor network and a Yuri-linked courier route.

A successful tail can also put Jim in contact with Rin or Ellie, or show him using a route that leads toward Yuri's operation. This gives the PCs access to the principal thieves without needing Sid's inventory first.
If he realizes he is being followed, he changes routes rather than instantly starting a fight.
Next leads: the graveyard tunnel, Yuri's courier network, or Rin/Ellie through a covert meeting or handoff.

entries.name: Green Grape
entries: Caela rents a small room above the Green Grape under a mundane pretext.
Concrete contents: a spare set of clothes, a small coin packet, a short shift-report written in abbreviated kitchen terms, and a payment chit tied to Yuri's tavern accounts.
The room should establish reporting and payment, not contain a villain confession. If the PCs never visit, move the essential payment clue onto Caela or another logical location.
Next leads: Yuri through the payment record; Caela if she is still at large; or Rin/Ellie if the reporting notes identify where material is handed off.

entries.name: Cal Stone
entries: Cal Stone is a coerced dwarf mason and tunnel witness. He is frightened and reluctant because Yuri pressured him into building parts of the hidden tunnel network.

How the PCs can find Cal: Sid can name him when asked about unusual masonry or tunnel work; inspection of a tunnel can reveal Cal's recognizable mason's mark or distinctive stonework; or a pressured conspirator can mention the frightened dwarf Yuri forced to build the passages.
Cal knows a tunnel access and can describe the hidden construction in practical detail. He also knows that Yuri personally commissioned and directed the work.

Cal can show the PCs the access at his barn and explain how the passages connect into the wider network. His testimony is a direct Yuri link, while the tunnel itself corroborates that an organized operation exists.
Cal is not a mastermind. Treat fear and self-protection as the obstacle, not deception for its own sake.
A failed social check can cost time or require reassurance/protection, but the PCs can still obtain both the tunnel route and the Yuri connection.
Next leads: enter the tunnel network, take Cal's testimony to Sid or the council, or use his description of Yuri's operation to pursue Rin and Ellie.

entries.name: Dagger Rock Tavern
entries: Yuri is composed, mildly offended by accusations, and careful not to overreact in public.
Routine questioning: he appears cooperative and quietly has the PCs watched.
Direct accusation: he frames the PCs as harassing a respectable proprietor and alerts his agents.

Watching the tavern, following a courier, or finding a hidden route can expose Rin or Ellie moving between Yuri's operation and the tunnel network. The PCs do not need Sid's stolen-goods list to discover them.

If Yuri concludes that the case against him is closing, his preferred endgame is not a stand-up fight in his own tavern. He shifts toward a final strike on the Happy Orc: plant stolen goods, burn part of the place, silence a witness, and escape through the tunnel network before Sid can lock the town down.
Next leads: Rin/Ellie, a tunnel route, or Yuri's reaction if the PCs confront him directly.

entries.name: Tunnel Discoveries
entries: Access can come from Grog's well, Jim's graveyard route, Cal's barn, or Yuri's wider hidden network.

A tunnel can identify Cal even if the PCs have never met Sid: sections of worked stone carry Cal's mason's mark or a distinctive construction technique recognizable to townsfolk as his work. Asking who built it points to Cal Stone.

Following the network toward Yuri's sphere can also reveal Rin or Ellie using the passages, a cache or handoff tied to them, or a route into their part of the operation. Sid is helpful but not required to reach the principal thieves.
For table play, you do not need to map the entire tunnel system. Use one small supplemental map: the Tunnel Chamber (Cellar Entrance) connected to the Happy Orc.
Finding a tunnel early is a success. Reward it by shortening the investigation and giving the PCs a better starting position for the finale.
Next leads: Cal Stone from the masonry; Rin/Ellie by following the network; or Yuri when the tunnel evidence is paired with testimony, records, or stolen property.

entries.name: Yuri's Reactions

entries.caption: Yuri's Response
rows: Stay publicly helpful; have agents watch the PCs.
Alert agents and begin quiet evidence movement.
Rin and Ellie start packing portable evidence and preparing a move against the Happy Orc.
Move evidence or plan an underground approach if Yuri plausibly learns about it.
Push the emergency frame-up plan at the Happy Orc.
Go directly to the endgame. Yuri reacts because the PCs have exposed the operation; do not manufacture extra mystery.

entries: The fictional trigger for the finale is player success, not the wall clock. Yuri launches the Happy Orc frame-up when he reasonably learns that the PCs have exposed an agent, secured testimony, uncovered decisive evidence, reached the tunnel network, turned the council, or otherwise threatened the survival of his scheme. The session clock only tells the DM when to accelerate clues so that this trigger can occur in time.

entries.name: Rewards / Evidence Gained

entries.caption: Evidence Strength
rows: Enough to investigate further, not enough to convict Yuri.
Stolen property/records from Rin and Ellie
Proves secret activity; pair with testimony, records, or stolen property.

entries: Never erase an essential clue because of one failed check.

data.name: Chapter 3: Return to the Happy Orc

entries.name: Maps

entries.caption: One-Map Finale Build
rows: Use only your modular walls plus AF634A pieces. Only add one custom cellar-entrance marker that you do not physically own.
Primary map for both the opening scene and the final confrontation.
Minimal build from walls and open space. Wall-built stalls are fine; AF634A crates/barrels are optional.
Use only if the fight spills out the rear exit.
Simple underground room. Use AF634A crates/barrels if desired plus the cellar-entrance marker.
Use only if the fight spills underground or a chase reaches the tunnel mouth.

entries: The main-floor tavern map stays on the table all session. The Stable / Yard and Tunnel Chamber are optional supplemental builds on your box top and bottom.

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: The finale returns to the Happy Orc. Once Yuri realizes through the PCs' successful investigation that the case is collapsing, he attempts one last frame-up there: plant stolen goods, start a fire or other chaos, destroy evidence, silence a witness, and escape through the rear or underground routes.
This chapter should feel like the adventure coming full circle: the place where the PCs met Grog becomes the place they save.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: Start this chapter because Yuri has a reason to believe the PCs are closing in—not merely because the clock reaches 1:40. The clock is a pacing backstop: if necessary, use Sid's hard lead or another fail-forward clue to create the success that provokes Yuri's response.

Do not stop to build an entirely new battle map. The Happy Orc should already be on the table. When the endgame begins, simply add enemies, civilians, smoke/fire markers if needed, and the cellar-entrance marker if it is not already visible.
If the players uncovered the tunnel angle, let that matter. They may anticipate the point of attack, guard the cellar entrance, cut off the rear exit, or split someone toward the Tunnel Chamber.
The Stable / Yard and Tunnel Chamber come out only if movement or objectives force the fight into those spaces.

entries.name: Approach Options
entries: Rush back to the Happy Orc once the PCs realize Yuri is making a move.
Lay a trap for Yuri's operatives at the Happy Orc and try to catch them planting evidence.
Guard the cellar entrance or rear exit while leaving the main room active for civilians and defenders.
Split forces between the main floor and the Stable / Yard or Tunnel Chamber if the enemies attempt multiple objectives at once.
If the players take the offensive against Yuri elsewhere, surviving conspirators or the final evidence move can still collapse back into a return-to-the-Happy-Orc confrontation.

entries.name: Simple NCFA-Style Tactical Map Key
entries: Treat the Happy Orc main floor as the tactical center. Important features are the front doors, rear exit, bar, open common-room floor, tables and chairs, fireplace, shelving, and the cellar entrance marker.

The Stable / Yard is a simple overflow zone for fleeing enemies, fire risk, or mounted/animal chaos. The Tunnel Chamber is a simple overflow zone for a last escape attempt, hidden contraband, or a short underground pursuit.
Do not overcomplicate the geography. One main room and two optional side zones are enough.

entries.name: Cellar Entrance and Tunnel Chamber
entries: The only non-owned feature in the tavern should be the custom cellar-entrance marker. That marker represents the route into the tunnel chamber and broader network.
The Tunnel Chamber does not need to represent the entire underground complex. It is simply the first underground room connected to the Happy Orc, with one or more off-map tunnel exits beyond it.
If the players never go below, you may resolve all underground pressure narratively and keep the fight entirely on the main tavern map.

entries.name: Yuri, Rin, and Ellie
entries: Default plan: Yuri appears personally only if the investigation has put him under real pressure. Otherwise Rin and Ellie lead the initial move and Yuri enters once the frame-up is underway or collapsing.

Rin focuses on planting or carrying stolen goods, threatening witnesses, or seizing evidence. Ellie focuses on control, confusion, concealment, and opening an escape path. Yuri focuses on turning the scene against Grog, then escaping once the attempt fails.
Grunt and Brock are excellent supporting bodies for this finale if you need more muscle or an obvious arson/intimidation wing.
For a four-PC table, Yuri/Rin/Ellie are the default core trio. Treat Grunt and Brock as scaling tools, not automatic participants.

entries.name: Evidence
entries: Possible decisive evidence in the finale includes: the Yuri-linked payment chit, portable records or satchels carried by Yuri or Rin, stolen goods being planted at the Happy Orc, and living witness testimony from captured conspirators.
If you want a concrete physical objective, let Rin carry a stolen-item bundle or evidence satchel toward the rear exit or cellar entrance.
Do not make the proof disappear off-screen. If Yuri wants it destroyed or moved, put it in a creature's hands or on the map.

entries.name: Running the Fight

entries.caption: Default Enemy Plan
rows: If present, Yuri directs the frame-up and looks for a path to blame Grog publicly.
Rin or Grunt/Brock move to plant goods, threaten a witness, or start the physical objective.
Ellie uses control, concealment, or confusion rather than maximum damage.
Yuri pivots toward escape once resistance hardens.
Rin grabs portable evidence or pushes toward the rear exit / cellar entrance.
Ellie blocks pursuit, covers retreat, or splits the PCs.
Yuri bargains, flees, or surrenders if the operation is lost.
Rin protects Ellie or tries one last objective push.
Ellie creates a final opening, then flees or yields.

entries: Do not repeatedly attack a downed PC. Once the PCs clearly control the civilians, evidence, and exits, the conspirators stop behaving like death-fight enemies.

entries.name: Objective-Based Combat
entries: Primary PC objectives: keep the Happy Orc from being successfully framed, protect civilians and staff, stop a fire or staged sabotage if one is in play, secure decisive evidence, and prevent Yuri or his agents from escaping.
Good moving objectives include: stop planted stolen goods from being hidden in the tavern, keep a witness alive, intercept the evidence satchel, cut off the rear exit, and block the cellar entrance.
If the PCs present overwhelming proof and demand surrender, the fight can become an interception or escape-prevention scene rather than a traditional slugfest.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: If the PCs stop the frame-up and secure the evidence, Grog is publicly cleared and Yuri's credibility collapses. Sid can move in for arrests and the town sees who really targeted the Happy Orc.
If Yuri escapes but the frame-up fails and evidence survives, the PCs still win the civic battle while leaving Yuri as a fugitive.
If the Happy Orc suffers damage but the conspiracy is exposed, let the emotional ending focus on who was protected, how Grog responds, and how the town's perception changes.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: No fixed cash or magic-item payout is established. The principal rewards are saving the Happy Orc, clearing Grog, exposing Yuri, and creating a satisfying full-circle ending.

entries.caption: Runtime NPCs
rows: Honest, procedural, frustrated by weak evidence.
Cautious mayor; wants order and defensible proof.
Optional civic/religious voice if players seek him out.
Coerced dwarf mason; knows tunnel access, recognizes his own construction, and testifies Yuri commissioned/directed the work.

entries.name: NPC Running Notes
entries: Grog is innocent. Sid is supportive but lawful. Yuri is calm and controlling. Rin and Ellie prioritize each other and survival. Caela, Jim, Grunt, and Brock are network links. Cal is the coerced dwarf mason and tunnel witness.
Do not let Grog or Sid overshadow the PCs in the finale. Grog should protect people and the tavern; Sid should secure the scene and make arrests. They are support, not extra party members.

entries.caption: Redundant Clues
rows: Deliberate stable fire; Grunt/Brock; Jim's rumors; Caela's reporting.
Caela payment; Jim trail; Rin/Ellie records; Cal testimony that Yuri commissioned/directed the tunnel work; Grunt/Brock testimony.
Grog's well; graveyard route; Cal's barn; Cal's mason's mark/workmanship; Yuri's hidden routes.
Rin and Ellie are principal thieves
Sid's stolen-goods comparison; Jim or Caela handoffs; following Grunt/Brock; tunnel surveillance; stolen goods; infiltration gear; records.
Grog says so; Sid defends him; Sid's records are accurate.
Sid supports Grog; Berik doubts the accusations; Logan wants fairness; Wes moves with solid proof.

entries.caption: Council
rows: Already believes Grog; needs enough evidence to act lawfully against Yuri.
Physical evidence or two corroborating witnesses.
One credible Yuri link plus reassurance he will not be left exposed.
Proof that Grog is being deliberately framed.

entries.name: Common Unexpected Approaches
entries: {@b Accuse Yuri immediately.} He stays composed, calls it harassment, and accelerates his final move against the Happy Orc.
{@b Attack Yuri immediately.} Sid intervenes if available. Otherwise the PCs create a legal complication, but the adventure continues through evidence, pursuit, arrest, surrender, or escape.
{@b Distrust Grog.} Let them investigate him. They can find ordinary flaws or tavern misconduct, but no organized-crime link.
{@b Zone of Truth.} Innocent NPCs cooperate. Conspirators can refuse, evade, answer narrowly, or leave. Refusal is informative but not proof.
{@b Detect Thoughts.} Let the spell work. It may shorten the mystery; in exchange Yuri becomes alerted sooner if the use is obvious or discovered.
{@b Speak with Animals.} Stable animals can confirm the fire was abnormal and point toward the men around the stable.
{@b Follow or capture Grunt/Brock.} This is a valid shortcut to Yuri, Jim, Caela, or the tunnel network.
{@b Expose Caela early.} Let her try to flee or warn Yuri. Her clue remains recoverable; Rin/Ellie begin moving evidence and preparing the Happy Orc endgame.

{@b Find a tunnel immediately.} Reward it. The masonry can point to Cal, and following the network can expose Rin/Ellie or Yuri's operation. Skip redundant investigation and let the PCs prepare for the cellar-entrance / tunnel aspect of the finale.
{@b Split the party.} Cut between groups every 5–8 minutes and converge their clues toward the same return-to-the-Happy-Orc endgame.
{@b Solve the case early.} Yuri reacts immediately because the PCs have threatened the scheme. Go to the finale; do not fake additional mystery or wait for the clock.
{@b Go to the council first.} Run a short social confrontation. If pressure turns against Yuri, he triggers the emergency frame-up plan at the Happy Orc.
{@b Recruit Grog or Sid.} They can protect civilians, secure exits, or handle arrests, but the PCs remain the people resolving the core objectives.
{@b Try to avoid combat.} Honor successful social play. The required Hall fight can become an interception, escape, evidence-rescue, or defense of the Happy Orc rather than a forced murder scene.

entries.name: Fail-Forward Costs
entries: An essential clue is never destroyed by one failed check.

Good costs: 10–15 minutes lost; Yuri becomes more alert; a witness demands protection or payment; the clue is incomplete; the clue arrives with a complication; the PCs form a misleading but testable assumption.
Do not invent false objective evidence because of a poor roll.

entries.name: Finale Scaling — Four PCs
entries: The level-8 row deliberately keeps Ellie as an Illusionist rather than upgrading her to Mage. The finale is already pressured by civilians, evidence, fire/sabotage, and escape objectives; Mage-level burst damage makes the encounter unnecessarily swingy.

entries.name: Party-Size Adjustments
entries: 3 PCs: use the row one level lower when practical, or downgrade Rin.
5 PCs: add Grunt or Brock if the PCs are dominating, or bring one in from the Stable / Yard or cellar route after round 1.
6 PCs: add both Grunt and Brock, or one of them plus an extra thug-equivalent body.
Mixed-level group: use the median level. If the spread between highest and lowest PC is 3 or more, choose the lower plausible row.

entries.name: Resource Check
entries: The finale assumes the party reaches it with most hit points and signature resources still available.
If Grunt/Brock became a full resource-draining combat, either downgrade Rin one step or have Ellie emphasize non-damage control instead of burst damage.
Do not add reinforcements merely because the players are winning quickly. The encounter's pressure comes from evidence and escape.

Grog and Sid are not default allied combatants. Grog protects patrons, handles hazards, or holds an off-map threat; Sid secures exits, protects civilians, and handles arrests. Only put either in normal initiative if the PCs create circumstances where their direct combat participation is necessary.

entries.name: One-Page Running Reference
entries: Baseline: four level-6 PCs; supported levels 4–8; 3-hour target; three investigation beats.

Truth: Yuri alone is mastermind. Grog is innocent. Sid is an ally. Rin/Ellie are principal thieves. Caela is the kitchen spy. Jim spreads rumors. Grunt/Brock handle arson/intimidation. Cal is the coerced dwarf mason who can tie Yuri directly to the tunnel construction.

Clock: 0:45 force a useful clue if needed; 1:00 ensure a Yuri link; 1:15 restate facts; 1:20 stop opening optional locations; by 1:40 use fail-forward clues so the PCs have achieved enough success to provoke Yuri's reaction; 1:50 initiative; 2:30 surrender/flight; 2:45 close.
Hard lead if stuck: Sid's inventory includes a silver-inlaid merchant's compass with a chipped green enamel lid; a witness ties a similar item to an elf matching Rin near Yuri's tavern.

Clue-web rule: every scene ends with an actionable next lead. Cal can be found through Sid, tunnel workmanship, or a pressured conspirator. Rin/Ellie can be reached through Sid, Jim, Caela, Grunt/Brock, or the tunnels.
Finale trigger: Yuri strikes the Happy Orc because the PCs have threatened the conspiracy—not because a timer expires. The clock only tells you when to accelerate clues.
Physical setup: one main Happy Orc map using only your walls and AF634A pieces, plus one custom cellar-entrance marker. Optional 8 × 6 Stable / Yard and 8 × 6 Tunnel Chamber builds only if needed.
Finale objective: keep the Happy Orc from being framed, protect civilians, secure evidence, and stop escape through the rear or cellar routes.
